# Independent SigV4 vectors

`vectors.json` was generated by unmodified `S3SigV4Auth` and
`S3SigV4QueryAuth` from AWS CLI **2.31.18**, source revision
`f4f66e65e70f23f1bf232ecb4a6d8696f4dda3bc`. The source archive SHA256 is
`0e164de8e225122efccfae85c989e5b47c2de8a3d1efc4e7bdfe02ac29827d73`;
the exact signer source SHA256 is embedded in the fixture and enforced by the
generator. This is the AWS reference pinned in the compatibility reference lock.
All credentials and tokens are synthetic.

The Python generator uses botocore's own canonical request, string-to-sign,
signature, and Authorization injection, with a fixed timestamp. Python's
`urllib.parse.quote` independently prepares RFC3986 keys and query values.
Presigns append auth parameters without botocore's dict-based preparation,
which would collapse duplicate names; the resulting request is passed through
botocore's actual query signer. No ESS signer or canonicalization code is used.
The generator records canonical requests so the expected byte-level input is
reviewable. These are cryptographic reference tests, not live AWS evidence.

To regenerate after capturing the pinned AWS source archive:

```sh
uv pip install --target /tmp/ess-sigv4-reference-deps python-dateutil==2.9.0.post0 six==1.17.0 urllib3==2.5.0 jmespath==1.0.1 awscrt==0.28.2
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/ess-cli-reference-m0/aws-cli-2.31.18/awscli:/tmp/ess-sigv4-reference-deps python3 apps/ex_storage_service_cli/test/fixtures/sigv4/generate.py
```

No Python packages are required when running the Elixir tests or CLI. Runtime
signing continues to use OTP SHA256 and HMAC; no Hex dependency was added.
SigV4a and aws-chunked/trailer signing remain separate later milestones.
